craft_claim: Indirection — meaning suggested beyond the literal statement — can carry philosophical weight, but suggestion must remain tethered to an arguable idea or it slides into vagueness.

supporting_evidence.note: Anandavardhana's dhvani theory holds that suggested meaning (dhvani) can outrank literal statement (abhidha) and metaphor (laksana); cross-links the existing shared claim clm-dhvani-suggestion-theory. Read-only shared source.

supporting_evidence.location: Passim, e.g. the seasonal and ruin imagery
supporting_evidence.note: Kenko lets images of impermanence suggest a general claim about conduct without stating it as a proposition.

counterevidence.note: Undirected suggestion is exactly what pseudo-profound receptivity rewards; suggestion can obscure rather than deepen when no arguable idea constrains it.

scope: Poetry, literary non-fiction, contemplative prose and image-led copy.
exceptions: In evidence-bearing academic L0, suggestive indirection must yield to explicit claim and locator; dhvani is not a licence for unsupported assertion.
